answer: Min-cut attestation quorum: an identity joins by collecting cross-cluster attestations, but each social-graph min-cut holds one vote, so clones behind a single cut pool into one slot. An attacker buying N identities must cross a widening ridge of distinct cuts, each demanding disjoint attestors; clones at one mesa or wharf share a vote, forcing fresh trust everywhere. Cost rises super-linearly: independent cuts need non-fungible attestor sets failing together.
